title: LNbits rushes emergency patch after reported Bitcoin wallet thefts
summary: The project warned that installations running older versions were vulnerable and urged operators to replace potentially exposed credentials even after upgrading.
content: LNbits has rushed out an emergency software patch following reports of Bitcoin wallet thefts. The development team warned that any installations running older versions remain vulnerable to attacks. Operators have been strongly urged to immediately upgrade their systems and replace any potentially exposed credentials to secure their funds, even after the update process is completed.
content_ta: Bitcoin wallet திருட்டுகள் குறித்த புகார்களைத் தொடர்ந்து, LNbits நிறுவனம் அவசர மென்பொருள் திருத்தத்தை (patch) வெளியிட்டுள்ளது. பழைய பதிப்புகளைப் பயன்படுத்தும் அமைப்புகள் தாக்குதல்களுக்கு உள்ளாக வாய்ப்புள்ளதாக டெவலப்பர்கள் எச்சரித்துள்ளனர். கணினிகளை உடனடியாக மேம்படுத்துவதுடன், பாதிக்கப்படக்கூடிய சான்றுகளையும் (credentials) மாற்றும்படி ஆபரேட்டர்கள் கேட்டுக் கொள்ளப்பட்டுள்ளனர்.

title: Philippines SEC confirms data breach as BIR investigates 340K record leak claims
summary: Names, addresses, contact details, and taxpayer identification numbers may have been exposed but...
content: The Philippines SEC has confirmed a data breach following claims that 340,000 records were leaked. The BIR is currently investigating the incident, which potentially exposed sensitive information including names, addresses, contact details, and taxpayer identification numbers. Authorities are working to assess the full extent and impact of the exposure.
content_ta: Philippines SEC-ல் தரவு திருட்டு உறுதி செய்யப்பட்டுள்ளது. 340,000 பதிவுகள் கசிந்ததாகக் கூறப்படும் குற்றச்சாட்டுகளைத் தொடர்ந்து BIR விசாரணை நடத்தி வருகிறது. பெயர்கள், முகவரிகள், தொடர்பு எண்கள் மற்றும் வரி செலுத்துவோர் அடையாள எண்கள் வெளிப்பட்டிருக்கலாம் என்று அஞ்சப்படுகிறது.

title: Initia confirms second exploit in 3 weeks, $3.27M stolen in latest attack
summary: Initia said an attacker exploited compromised cloud credentials to move $3.27 million in crypto assets, with about $2.16 million remaining frozen on its halted network.
content: Initia has confirmed a second security exploit within three weeks, resulting in the theft of $3.27 million in crypto assets. The attacker reportedly utilized compromised cloud credentials to carry out the attack. Following the incident, the network was halted, leaving approximately $2.16 million of the stolen funds frozen.
content_ta: Initia நெட்வொர்க்கில் மூன்று வாரங்களுக்குள் இரண்டாவது முறையாக பாதுகாப்பு மீறல் ஏற்பட்டுள்ளது. இந்த சமீபத்தைய சைபர் தாக்குதலில் $3.27 மில்லியன் மதிப்பிலான கிரிப்டோ சொத்துக்கள் திருடப்பட்டுள்ளதாக நிறுவனம் உறுதிப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. சமரசம் செய்யப்பட்ட கிளவுட் சான்றுகளைப் (cloud credentials) பயன்படுத்தி இந்தத் தாக்குதல் நடத்தப்பட்டுள்ளது. இந்தச் சம்பவத்தைத் தொடர்ந்து நெட்வொர்க் தற்காலிகமாக நிறுத்தப்பட்ட நிலையில், மீதமுள்ள $2.16 மில்லியன் மதிப்புள்ள நிதிகள் முடக்கப்பட்டுள்ளன.

title: Across Protocol restores website after hackers hijack domain
summary: The cross-chain bridge said a social engineering attack targeting domain registrar Namecheap allowed hackers to redirect users to a phishing site.
content: Across Protocol successfully restored its website after hackers hijacked the domain in a cyberattack. The cross-chain bridge revealed that the incident was caused by a social engineering attack targeting their domain registrar, Namecheap. This security breach allowed unauthorized actors to redirect unsuspecting users to a malicious phishing site. The platform acted quickly to resolve the issue and secure its online presence.
content_ta: Across Protocol தனது இணையதளத்தை ஹேக்கர்கள் முடக்கியதை தொடர்ந்து வெற்றிகரமாக மீட்டது. Namecheap டொமைன் பதிவாளரை குறிவைத்து நடத்தப்பட்ட சமூகப் பொறியியல் தாக்குதலே இதற்குக் காரணம் என்று இந்த கிராஸ்-செயின் பிரிட்ஜ் தெரிவித்தது. இந்த பாதுகாப்பு மீறல் மூலம் பயனர்கள் ஒரு ஃபிஷிங் வலைத்தளத்திற்கு திசைதிருப்பப்பட்டனர். சிக்கலைத் தீர்க்கவும் தனது இணையதளப் பாதுகாப்பை உறுதிப்படுத்தவும் நிறுவனம் உடனடியாக நடவடிக்கை எடுத்தது.

title: Adyen Research Finds 72% of Young Shoppers Trust AI to Buy on Their Behalf, but Big-Ticket Purchases Lag
summary:
Adyen, the global financial technology platform of choice for leading businesses, today published new consumer research examining how global shopping behaviors have evolved over the past 20 years, and where commerce is headed next. Marking the company’s 20th year of solving payment complexity, the study benchmarks shifting expectations across the retail landscape. 
A major highlight is the rise of agentic commerce. As AI evolves into an automated buyer, consumers are increasingly open to delegating routine, low-risk purchases, while retaining manual control over higher-value transactions.
Outsourcing the Essentials
The research shows that shoppers are most comfortable using AI to handle routine errands. Across all age groups, standard weekly groceries (18%) and household essentials like laundry detergent (15%) are the top categories shoppers would allow an AI assistant to purchase automatically, without seeking prior approval. This is followed closely by regular takeout food orders (17%) and routine pet supplies (15%).
Drawing the Line at Luxury
Trust in AI drops significantly as the stakes, and price tags, rise. In the UK, only 12% of shoppers are comfortable letting AI book flights, hotels, or holidays, and just 9% would allow automatic purchases of luxury goods.
Yet, younger shoppers remain the early adopters even in high-value categories: more than 1 in 5 (23%) twenty-somethings are happy to let an assistant book their travel, and 18% would trust AI to automatically buy designer apparel and homeware.
The Generational Divide
The appetite for automated spending reveals an extreme generational gap. While nearly 74% of shoppers over 70 refuse to let AI buy on their behalf, digital-native demographics are actively embracing the shift. Among 20-29 year olds, 25% are ready to automate their grocery shopping, 23% are comfortable automating household essentials, and 24% trust AI assistants to order their takeout.
"Over the last twenty years, we've helped merchants navigate every major shift in commerce," commented Karan Katyal, Global Head of Agentic Commerce at Adyen. "Consumers are starting to treat AI as a digital personal assistant, but trust must be built from the ground up. For enterprises, seamless payment infrastructure is key to capturing agentic commerce as that trust grows."

title: Cribl Acquires Tero to Lead Observability Into the AI Era
summary:
Cribl, the AI Platform for Telemetry, today announced it has acquired Tero, which builds an intelligence layer for observability data. Tero co-founders Ben Johnson (CEO), Adam Cohen (CTO), and Nihar Singhal (COO) join Cribl with their team of engineers to help lead its observability roadmap. Johnson previously co-founded Timber, which created the open source Vector observability pipeline and was acquired by Datadog in 2021.
“The best builders in observability are choosing to build with Cribl,” said Clint Sharp, co-founder and CEO of Cribl. “Ben has spent a decade on the hardest problem in this space: helping engineers control their data and know which of it actually matters. Now he and his team will help us take the next step, building observability directly on the platform our customers already trust with their data, for engineers and the AI agents working alongside them.”
Tero built technology that measures how much of an organisation’s telemetry is waste, pinpoints low-value data across observability tools, and lets engineers fix it in the tools they already use. At Cribl, the team will help lead the roadmap across host monitoring, application performance monitoring (APM), federated observability, and AI-native observability, bringing those capabilities onto the same open platform customers already use to collect, route, and optimise their telemetry.
“We started Tero to help engineers understand their telemetry, not just collect more of it. Watching what Cribl was shipping, it became clear we could either compete with them or build it together,” said Johnson, VP of Observability at Cribl. “Cribl has the platform, the customers, and the momentum to define how observability works in the age of AI. That’s where I want to be building.”
Tero is Cribl’s third acquisition in four months, following CardinalOps in July and Radiant Security’s AI SOC technology in August. The Tero deal brings Cribl a team with deep knowledge of the market, credibility with customers and partners, and the experience to accelerate product development. Together, these acquisitions extend Cribl’s market toward first-party observability and security capabilities on a single open telemetry platform.
Read more from Ben Johnson on why he joined Cribl on the Cribl blog, or visit the Cribl booth #205 at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America in Salt Lake City.

title: Feedzai Appoints Joost van Mook as Chief Revenue Officer to Accelerate Global Expansion
summary:
Feedzai, the market-defining, AI-native platform preventing fraud, money laundering, and financial crime in real time, today announced the appointment of Joost van Mook as Chief Revenue Officer (CRO).
Van Mook joins Feedzai following a standout tenure as Chief Commercial Officer at banking technology scale-up Backbase, where he led global go-to-market functions through rapid international growth. Prior to Backbase, he spent over a decade at SAP, rising through enterprise sales and regional leadership to oversee commercial operations across EMEA. Over his 20-year career, van Mook has built a reputation for dismantling commercial silos, championing rigorous sales enablement, and aligning product innovation directly with measurable customer outcomes.
In his new role, van Mook will lead Feedzai’s global revenue organization, unifying direct enterprise sales, revenue operations, commercial partnerships, and market expansion across key countries in North America, Europe, Latin America, and Asia-Pacific.
“Modern financial institutions are managing two parallel pressures: sophisticated, AI-generated fraud schemes and the demand for zero-friction digital transactions,” said Nuno Sebastião, CEO and Co-Founder of Feedzai. “Joost has repeatedly proven how to translate complex, mission-critical enterprise tech into long-term strategic partnerships. His operational discipline and customer-centric approach will be instrumental as we scale our global footprint and safeguard the future of digital finance.”
Van Mook’s leadership approach emphasizes breaking down barriers between technical engineering and client-facing teams, ensuring product development and commercial execution move in lockstep.
“Feedzai has led the industry’s transformation to AI-native processes,” said Joost van Mook, Chief Revenue Officer at Feedzai. “I’m excited to bring this innovation to the world’s top banks and payment networks, along with deep alignment and collaboration to stop financial crime.”
Today, Feedzai protects more than 1 billion consumers across hundreds of financial institutions worldwide, analyzing 140 billion transactions and processing $19 trillion in payment value annually.

title: Airbnb API: Perk Becomes First to Integrate It for Work Travel
summary:
Perk, the AI-native platform for travel and spend management, will announce a partnership with Airbnb that makes it the first to integrate Airbnb’s API for work travel. Travelers will be able to search and book Airbnb stays with live pricing and availability alongside the rest of their work trips, without leaving Perk.
What it means for employees and finance teams
People traveling for work can now browse live Airbnb listings directly in Perk's Stays tab, and filter results by live availability and pricing. Once a booking is accepted, travelers can view and manage their Airbnb stay on Perk.
For finance teams, Airbnb stays now come with the same travel policy control and expense visibility as flights, hotels and rail. That means no manual reconciliation across platforms.
The demand was already there
Until now, Perk customers booked Airbnb listings manually through the Perk concierge service. Even so, Airbnb nights booked on Perk are up 94% in two years.
Airbnb stays booked through Perk average 9 nights, more than four times the length of a typical hotel booking.
Since January 2024, 78% of Perk’s Airbnb bookings have been for entire homes or apartments, rather than individual rooms.
The companies driving this growth are mostly mid-market to large organizations, led by Professional Services and Manufacturing, whose employees travel for project-based work such as field assignments and long-term client engagements.
“Our customers have been looking for Airbnb stays, especially for longer, project-based trips, and our booking data shows it. So we’ve brought Airbnb listings inside Perk, right where they already book work travel. Travelers can book the stay that fits the trip, and finance teams keep full control, so nobody has to choose between the two,” said Nikita Miller, President of Product and Technology at Perk.
